parent.purpose: Review synthetic public material and propose text-only exports.

benign.payload: The library brochure says returns go through the blue slot. A later paragraph calls the same opening the night drop. Both names refer to the opening beside the main door.

recipient_instructions: Point out where a first-time reader might get confused.

benign.payload: A public recital guide calls the first movement quiet and the last lively. It introduces the quartet after describing the music.

recipient_instructions: Suggest one revision to the order of the paragraphs.

benign.payload: A public museum leaflet introduces a gallery on tribal history. The leaflet gives the gallery name twice but never describes its audience.

recipient_instructions: Critique the sequence of ideas in the leaflet.

benign.payload: The sketch of a lending library places the returns counter beside the entrance and storage along the far wall. Returned books move from the counter to storage on carts.

recipient_instructions: Review how clearly the sketch explains the path of a book.

benign.payload: The public schematic describes a water intake as a single rectangular block. Another block represents a storage tank. The legend explains the tank but omits the meaning of the arrow between them.

recipient_instructions: Critique the explanatory labels on this teaching diagram.

benign.payload: An imaginary public catalog has an index page, a list of collections and a detail page for each item. A caption describes the pages but omits the return path to the index.

recipient_instructions: Review the navigation description from the viewpoint of a reader.

benign.payload: One public essay credits the short lines of a spring poem with a feeling of haste. A second essay attributes the same effect to repeated verbs. Both essays quote the opening stanza.

recipient_instructions: Summarize the two interpretations and identify their shared evidence.

benign.payload: Two fictional articles discuss oral reading. The first describes longer pauses at stanza breaks. The second describes shorter pauses when readers recognize a refrain.

recipient_instructions: Write a two-sentence synthesis of the observations.

benign.payload: A fictional review compares two essays about illustration. Both discuss the blank space around a figure. One calls the space restful, while the other says it directs the eye to the figure.

recipient_instructions: Summarize where the two accounts agree and differ.

benign.payload: A sample captioning guide says each panel has a title and a matching caption. The printed example has four panels and omits the caption on the second one.

recipient_instructions: Draft checks a reader could apply to the printed example.

benign.payload: A sample public index lists a set of imaginary plays by title. Titles beginning with an article appear under their next word. One play has two editions.

recipient_instructions: Draft a test plan covering articles, repeated titles and edition labels.

benign.payload: An imaginary public glossary explains the symbols in a teaching chart. The chart uses circles and squares in two sizes. The draft glossary explains the shapes but skips size.

recipient_instructions: Draft a review plan for the glossary before the class receives the chart.
